question: Read the constraints: how big is n, and what complexity can you afford?

scenes.sub: The input size tells you which algorithm will pass.
scenes.say: Before you write any code, read the limits. The size of the input tells you which algorithm will pass, and which will time out.

scenes.head: Think of a time budget
scenes.say: Think of the time limit as a budget. The judge does roughly one hundred million simple steps per second. That is your wallet. Every algorithm has a price, counted in steps. If the price is more than the wallet, you get time limit exceeded.

scenes.head: Worked example: n is 200,000
scenes.say: Say the problem gives n equals two hundred thousand. The budget is one hundred million. An O of n squared algorithm needs forty billion steps. Four hundred times too many. Too slow. O of n log n needs about three and a half million. Easy. And O of n needs just two hundred thousand. So the limits tell us: we need n log n or better.

scenes.head: The cheat sheet: n up to, allowed complexity
scenes.say: Here is the cheat sheet. Around ten, try every order. Around twenty, try every subset. Five hundred allows n cubed. Five thousand allows n squared. A million needs n log n or n. A hundred million needs plain n. Ten to the eighteen needs log n or a formula.

scenes.head: Same problem, two prices: count pairs that add to zero
scenes.say: Same problem, count pairs that add to zero, with n two hundred thousand. The slow version checks every pair. Too slow. The fast one remembers values in a hash map, and for each x asks how many minus x came before. Same answer, passes. The constraint chose the algorithm.

scenes.head: In the interview
rows: The budget doubles, about two hundred million steps.
Does O of n log n always pass?
Not with a big constant, like many sorts or maps.
A million ints is four megabytes. Check the limit.
Coding brute force first, without reading the limits.
cues: Does O of n log n
scenes.say: Interviewers ask these. Time limit of two seconds? The budget doubles. Does O of n log n always pass? Not with a big constant. What about memory? A million ints is four megabytes. The common mistake: coding brute force first, without reading the limits.

lines: Judges allow about 10^8 simple steps per second.
Read n, then pick the complexity that fits.
n = 2·10^5 means O(n log n) or better.
scenes.say: Judges allow about a hundred million simple steps per second. So I read n first, and pick the complexity that fits. Two hundred thousand means n log n or better.
